q.e: When an apnea of prematurity episode does not self-correct within 10 seconds and fails to respond to tactile stimulation (tickling feet/stroking abdomen), brief oropharyngeal suctioning with repeat stimulation, and slight neck extension, the next step is to apply bag-and-mask ventilation using the O2% that the infant was receiving before the episode (not 100%). Intubation or nasal NPPV is considered only if there is still no response to bag-and-mask ventilation. (Heuer & Rodriguez 4th ed., lines 31246–31260)
q.src: Stepwise management of acute apnea of prematurity

sections.title: Clinical judgment · Neonatal: respiratory distress syndrome

q.q: A 35-week, 2,100-g newborn in the NICU has tachypnea (68 breaths/min), intercostal retractions, and central cyanosis on room air. To help differentiate pulmonary shunting due to infant respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) from an intracardiac right-to-left shunt due to a critical congenital heart defect (CCHD), the team performs a hyperoxia test by administering 100% oxygen for 10 minutes. Which of the following arterial blood gas results after 10 minutes on 100% oxygen would indicate that a pulmonary shunt such as RDS (rather than a CCHD) is the likely cause?
o: PaO2 > 200 torr (such as a PaO2 of 235 torr)
PaO2 < 150 torr (such as a PaO2 of 65 torr)
PaO2 between 150 and 200 torr (such as 170 torr)
PaO2 unchanged from room air (such as 42 torr)
q.e: In the hyperoxia test (assessing PaO2 after 10 minutes of breathing 100% O2), a PaO2 > 200 torr indicates that a pulmonary right-to-left shunt (such as RDS or PPHN) is likely. A PaO2 < 150 torr on 100% O2 indicates that an intracardiac right-to-left shunt (CCHD) is likely, whereas a PaO2 between 150 and 200 torr is inconclusive. (Heuer & Rodriguez 4th ed., lines 30891–30896, 31301–31306)

q.q: A 28-week, 1,050-g preterm neonate with respiratory distress syndrome is intubated in the NICU and ordered to receive rescue exogenous surfactant via endotracheal instillation. A chest radiograph has confirmed proper endotracheal tube placement, the airway has been suctioned clear of secretions, and continuous ECG and SpO2 monitoring are in place. Which of the following techniques should the respiratory therapist use when instilling the surfactant?
o: Insert a 5-Fr catheter to the ETT tip, split the dose between dependent bronchi, and manually ventilate 1–2 min
Pass a catheter beyond the ETT tip with the infant in Trendelenburg and perform endotracheal suctioning after 5 min
Dilute the surfactant in 10 mL of sterile water, instill as a single bolus while supine, and apply CPAP immediately
Deliver the surfactant via an in-line vibrating mesh nebulizer placed on the dry side of the heated humidifier
q.e: When instilling endotracheal surfactant for infant RDS, use a 5-Fr feeding tube or suction catheter inserted up to, but not past, the tip of the ETT; split the dose in half and instill half into each dependent bronchus (turning the infant from side to side); manually ventilate for 1–2 minutes afterward; and avoid suctioning for 6 hours if possible. Passing the catheter beyond the ETT tip and diluting with 10 mL of sterile water apply to L-E-A-N emergency drug instillation, not surfactant. (Heuer & Rodriguez 4th ed., lines 18740–18770)

q.q: A 27-week, 950-g preterm infant with severe respiratory distress syndrome complicated by pulmonary interstitial emphysema is being ventilated on a high-frequency oscillatory ventilator (CareFusion 3100A) with frequency 12 Hz, %I-time 33%, power/amplitude 3, mean airway pressure (Pmean) 14 cm H2O, and FiO2 0.55. Arterial blood gas analysis reveals pH 7.16, PaCO2 68 torr, and PaO2 62 torr. To lower the PaCO2 and improve the pH during high-frequency oscillatory ventilation, which of the following adjustments should the respiratory therapist recommend?
o: Increase the power/amplitude (ΔP) or decrease the oscillation frequency (Hz)
Decrease the power/amplitude (ΔP) or increase the oscillation frequency (Hz)
Increase the FiO2 to 0.80 while decreasing the inspiratory time to 25%
Decrease the mean airway pressure (Pmean) from 14 to 10 cm H2O
q.e: In infant RDS, permissive hypercapnia allows PaCO2 to rise only as long as the pH remains higher than 7.20; at pH 7.16, ventilation must be increased to lower PaCO2. During HFOV, PaCO2 is lowered primarily by increasing the power/amplitude (ΔP) or by decreasing the oscillation frequency (Hz) (or increasing %I-time), whereas Pmean and FiO2 primarily control oxygenation. (Heuer & Rodriguez 4th ed., lines 17410–17420, 17515–17540, 31330–31335)
